claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used to produce a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Conventional alloys are the initial material state.
Replacing conventional alloys with compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys is the proposed intervention.
The relevant behavior occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Alloy composition is the structural mediator connecting material replacement to the proposed behavior.
Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems resist temper embrittlement.
The predicted outcome is a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Conventional alloys exhibit temper embrittlement and constitute the baseline.
There is a temperature range in which temper embrittlement occurs.

contradictions.description: Temper-embrittlement resistance would suppress the proposed brittle regime, whereas the predicted ductile-brittle-ductile sequence requires an intervening brittle regime; no alternative source of that regime is provided.

The hypothesis proposes a ductile-brittle-ductile transition, but the falsification rule treats observation of temper embrittlement in the relevant alloy systems as falsifying. If temper embrittlement is intended to generate the brittle portion of the transition, these statements are inconsistent; no distinction between mechanisms is supplied.
